name: Spatial Importance Map via Unsharp Masking
definition: A spatial importance map is a 3D volume representing the saliency or boundary information of the input data, computed as the difference between the original intensity values and a low-pass filtered copy (unsharp mask). It captures salient and separability information about regions in the volume.
summary: Spatial Importance Map via Unsharp Masking computes a 3D boundary saliency map by subtracting original volume intensity from a blurred version, relying solely on input intensity rather than radiance to enable lighting-independent preprocessing.
